questions.explanation:

following benzodiazepines could be used if required for his treatment?
questions.explanation:
RaIsed AST and ALT levels suggest possible hepatic impiarment. In terms of sedation, drugs like Lorazepam, Oxazepam and Temazepam are
recommended for the treatments of patients with hepatic impairment. These drugs have short half life with no active metabolites. Use low
doses with caution, as sedative drugs can precipitate hepatic encephalopathy.

A 4-year-old boy was brought in to the clinic, as his mother was concerned about his sleepwalking problem. Which of the following
statements is incorrect regarding sleepwalking?

options.text: Child usually wakes up during sleep walking
It seems to run in families
Injury may occur during sleep walking
It typically occurs between the ages of 4 and 8
Sleep walking is common in children

correct_answer.text: Child usually wakes up during sleep walking

questions.explanation:
Sleepwalking can start at any age, but is more common in children. It's thought that at least 20% of children will sleepwalk at least once.
Sleepwalking mostly happens in childhood, typically between the ages of 4 and 8.The exact cause of sleepwalking is unknown, but it seems
to run in families. The child or the person usually has no recollection of the episode the following morning. Injury may occur like falling down
the stairs etc. Eyes are usually wide open and talk is incoherent with communication usually impossible. If awakened during the episode,
they are confused and disorientated.

questions.question_text: A 7-year-old boy presented with motor tics with facial grimacing for 1 year. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
The predominant manifestation in tic disorders is some form of tic. A tic is an involuntary, rapid, recurrent, non-rhythmic motor movement
(usually involving circumscribed muscle groups), or vocal production, that is of suddent onset and serves no apparent purpose. The absence
of vocal tics in this patient makes a diagnosis of Tourette's syndrome unlikely. The duration of at least a year makes chronic motor tics the
most likely diagnosis.

line drug. It is a noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor. It is not a controlled drug and a non stimulant. Co-morbid psychiatric illness is more
common in ADHD children (Ref: Fundamentals of Clinical Psychopharmacology;126)

Imprinting of the same region on chromosome 15 has been implicated for 2 conditions- Angelman and Prader-Willi syndromes. It is the loss

The presentation is suggestive of Neuroleptic malignant syndrome. It is important to avoid any agents thought to be causative especially

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding suicide in elderly population?

options.text: Older patients who self-harm are at more risk of completion of suicide
The usual mode of suicide is hanging

In the older population, females are at higher risk than males

correct_answer.text: Older patients who self-harm are at more risk of completion of suicide

younger people. A higher proportion of attempts are genuine attempts to die. Males are 3-4 times more likely to commit suicide. There is no
clear association between dementia and suicide in older people. Depressive illness is present in 2/3rds of completed suicide. (Ref: Oxford
handbook-Old age Psychiatry-102)

questions.question_text:
During a psychotherapy session a women with borderline personality disorder is asked to concentrate on what her partner was feeling

Mentalizing is the process by which we make sense of each other and ourselves, implicitly and explicitly, in terms of subjective states and
mental processes. It is a profoundly social construct in the sense that we are attentive to the mental states of those we are with, physically
or psychologically. Mentalization based treatment (MBT) is a time-limited treatment which structures interventions that promote the further
development of mentalizing. It has been tested in research trials and found to be an e�ective treatment for Borderline personality Disorder
when delivered by mental health professionals given limited additional training and with moderate levels of supervision(Ref: Mentalization
based treatment for borderline personality disorder: Bateman &Fonagy: World Psychiatry. 2010 Feb; 9(1): 11–15)

options.text: Shows a positive response to therapy

questions.explanation:

situation of psychotherapy where the patient may 'split' the psychotherapist for periods of time, seeing him/her as all good or all bad.

When faced with a stressor, a person evaluates the potential threat (primary appraisal). Primary appraisal is a person's judgment about the

e�orts aimed at regulation of the problem give rise to outcomes of the coping process. The Transactional Model of Stress and Coping is a
framework for evaluating how one copes with stressful events.

Indicated interventions target high-risk individuals with minimal but detectable signs or symptoms foreshadowing mental disorder, but who
do not meet diagnostic levels e.g identi�cation of a preschizophrenic state/prodrome of schizophrenia.
Selective interventions are targeted to individuals or subgroups whose risk of developing disorder is signi�cantly higher than average.

approaches are secondary prevention methods.
Tertiary prevention helps an individual to attain his or her full developmental potential through rehabilitation, which includes education,
support, environmental adjustments and aids.
